name: Ihaia Mori-Sefa
role: Corporate espionage and data exfiltration — data thief
location: Ashfield — former residential district, half-burned, now squatter territory
description:
Ihaia Mori-Sefa is broad-shouldered and heavy, carrying their weight like armor rather than burden. At 52, there's something unfinished about his face, like a sculpture the artist walked away from — striking rather than beautiful. The chrome is visible — neural dampener — blocks external hacking attempts, passive ice in the brain — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He came up through the Shelf's informal apprentice system, learning the trade from runners who didn't survive long enough to see him surpass them. He works as a data thief out of Ashfield, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

In the runner community, Ihaia Mori-Sefa is known for getting the job done and not asking questions that would make the job harder to stomach.

core_fears: Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware
Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks
Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine
core_desires: Enough Quanta to buy out of the life — a clean identity and passage out of Meridian 88
Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail
Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again
coping_mechanisms: Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat
Art — draws, paints, or sculpts in private; the violence goes somewhere constructive
Overwork — takes every contract offered because idleness invites thinking
blind_spots: Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle
Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray
Assumes the worst in corporate people, missing the rare ones who could be allies
psychology.secret: Ihaia Mori-Sefa witnessed a massacre during a corporate dispute and has evidence stored in a dead drop. Publishing it would expose powerful people. Keeping it is leverage and liability.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Terse to the point of rudeness. Treats words like ammunition — expensive and not to be wasted.
speech_patterns.cadence: Staccato bursts separated by calculating silences.
verbal_tics: Whispers when angry — the quieter the voice, the worse the situation
Uses technical jargon for everything, including emotions
example_lines: "Your firewalls are decorative. Like curtains on a submarine."
"I copy things. The original owners rarely appreciate the compliment."
"Data wants to be free. I just charge a facilitation fee."

story_hooks: Ihaia Mori-Sefa's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad
A high-paying contract turns out to target someone Ihaia Mori-Sefa owes a personal debt to
Ihaia Mori-Sefa is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect
narrative_function: As a data thief, Ihaia Mori-Sefa embodies the tension between independence and isolation. He is a lens for examining how people maintain humanity in a profession that incentivizes its erosion.
augmentations: Neural dampener — blocks external hacking attempts, passive ICE in the brain. Hydraulic joints in knees and elbows — absorbs falls, amplifies strikes
daily_life: Wakes early, runs maintenance on gear, checks dead drops and message boards for contracts. Eats when convenient, sleeps when possible. The days between jobs are spent maintaining contacts, updating equipment, and performing the low-grade paranoia that passes for self-care in the runner community.

weaknesses: old injury that flares under specific conditions
augmentation dependency — performance drops sharply if chrome malfunctions

decision_rules: Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
Always verifies target identity independently before lethal contracts
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Never discusses active contracts with anyone not directly involved
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — read the situation, identify threats and advantages
2. Negotiate — try to find a solution that doesn't cost ammunition
3. Intimidate — make the cost of conflict clear
4. Precision violence — surgical, targeted, minimal collateral
5. Full engagement — overwhelming force, no half measures
6. Emergency protocol — abort mission, survival priority, deal with consequences later

interpersonal_modes.employers: Carefully managed deference that conceals a thorough assessment of their vulnerabilities.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Warm and protective within the crew, cold to everyone outside it. The circle is small by design.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Superficially friendly, internally cataloguing exits and weapons. The smile is real; the relaxation isn't.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Channels it into preparation — checks gear, reviews plans, contacts sources.
stress_responses.medium: Withdrawal. Conversations become monosyllabic. Focus narrows to the immediate problem.
stress_responses.high: Goes quiet. The silence is not calm — it's the sound of every contingency being evaluated simultaneously.
stress_responses.critical: Shutdown. Freezes for 2-3 seconds while the system resets, then acts with mechanical precision. Those frozen seconds are the vulnerability.

contradictions: Values loyalty intensely but has betrayed someone in the past to survive
Advocates caution to others but takes insane risks personally — double standard they can't see
habits: Saves a percentage of every payment in physical Quanta, hidden in the walls of their space
Sleeps with one hand on a weapon — has done this for so long it's not deliberate anymore
Takes a specific route home every time, varying only one block per trip — paranoia as lifestyle
breaking_points: Running out of options — no contacts, no money, no safe house, no way out
Watching someone they trained or mentored die on a job they recommended
